source.title: MultiMem: Measuring and Mitigating Memorization in Multi-Modal Contrastive Learning
source.authors: Wen-Hao Wang; Franziska Boenisch; Michael Backes; Adam Dziedzic

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including appendix, is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests the effect of removing highly memorized training samples on downstream performance using MultiMem, a different memorization measure and multimodal contrastive models.
record.gate_note: The paper reports separate results for removal counts and metrics in Figure 5, but the supplied text describes the outcome in aggregate. Figure 5 also compares selection methods; only removal of samples selected by MultiMem bears on V8. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study measures memorization of cross-modal consistency, rather than the label-prediction memorization specified by V8. It removes samples and continues fine-tuning an already trained model, rather than retraining without them. Its performance improvements therefore do not test or challenge V8. No other version is tested.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that MultiMem captures global multimodal memorization, identify semantic misalignment across modalities as a major driver, and report that targeted mitigation during training or post-training removal followed by fine-tuning reduces memorization and improves downstream performance.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a leave-one-out cross-modal consistency measure and multimodal contrastive models; post-training mitigation removes selected samples and fine-tunes the model. The paper does not test the original classification setting.
record.method_sensitivity: The removal count changes the reported performance pattern; the text says improvement occurs when fewer than 500 samples are removed, with no clear improvement for random removal.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing fewer than 500 MultiMem-ranked samples and fine-tuning AudioCLIP for 25 additional epochs improves retrieval, linear-probe classification, and zero-shot classification; random removal has no clear improvement trend.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Removing examples with high cross-modal consistency memorization before continued fine-tuning can improve multimodal contrastive model performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Across representation-noise experiments, global MultiMem is negatively associated with retrieval performance, while memorization measures restricted to modality subsets do not consistently track it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Global cross-modal memorization can correlate negatively with retrieval generalization in multimodal contrastive models.

record.problems: The removal results are reported through plots without numeric values in the supplied text; no uncertainty estimates are stated. The experiment uses AudioCLIP and multimodal retrieval/classification metrics rather than V8's ResNet-50 test accuracy setting.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 5 also plots selection methods using CLIPMem, cosine similarity, and random selection, plus separate training-time mitigation results. Those are not rows for V8's removal operation. No per-count numeric outcomes could be recovered from the supplied text.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting versus natural-label held-out accuracy under the same architectures and training recipes.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizer generalization under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Magnitude-aware sharpness rankings of training-test gaps.
Removing examples ranked by their inclusion's effect on predicting their own labels, retraining, and comparing test-accuracy losses with equal-count random removal.

record.verdict_notes: A shared leave-one-out framework does not make cross-modal consistency memorization equivalent to label-prediction memorization. The reversed states and V8 challenge verdict in the record conflate these constructs. The supplied Figure 5 text does not recover individual curve values; axis ticks alone cannot supply them.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep past the interpolation threshold and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Large versus small batch generalization under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to training-test gaps.
ResNet-50, CIFAR-100 and ImageNet; test accuracy; comparison with removing the same number of random examples.
